editorial.summary: The episode begins by contrasting Asa Akira's experience of highly produced radio bits with DVDASA's aspiration to `real talk`, then tests that ideal through David's attempt to speak candidly with his aging father about mortality, marriage, sex, grandchildren, art and family history. Other cast members compare closeness, migration, language barriers, caregiving and parental acceptance. The second half broadens into pornography as work, future careers, the Ranch media diet, private sexual stories and trivia. Candid speech is preserved but not treated as automatically true; private relatives, medical histories and nonparticipants remain outside public discovery.
source_notes: The raw file contains 3,044 segments and approximately 23,559 words; the clean file contains 3,034 segments and approximately 23,563 words across 7,648.6 seconds.

The cleaner logs one enormous degenerate `line` run and ten empty zero-duration artifacts. Eleven logged edits produce a net ten-segment reduction because the degenerate run is replaced by one honest indistinct-audio marker.

The conversation repeatedly calls the game `today's Super Bowl`. NFL's official record dates Super Bowl XLVIII, Seattle Seahawks versus Denver Broncos, to February 2, 2014. The archive release date therefore should not be assumed to equal the recording date: https://www.nfl.com/news/super-bowl-xlviii-faq-everything-you-need-to-know-0ap2000000317294

NFL records Seattle's 43–8 win; the early discussion occurs before or during that game and is chronology evidence, not sports analysis: https://www.nfl.com/news/seahawks-crush-broncos-for-first-super-bowl-win-0ap2000000322949

The episode itself is the primary source for Asa's account of the Bubba radio production, her parents, work and future. Those are first-person claims, not a license to externally identify private relatives.
The public film correction at the end is important: the town painted red is in `High Plains Drifter`; `The Outlaw Josey Wales` supplies the Ten Bears dialogue.

The episode's offensive, explicit, coercive, implausible, contradictory and wrong ideas remain represented. Restrictions protect private relatives, health/reproductive detail, intimate images and nonparticipants; they do not censor ideas.
